theorems.name: Recovering S from mu
theorems.conditions: S differentiable, strictly positive on the interval.
theorems.intuition: The force of mortality is a logarithmic derivative of S; integrating and exponentiating undoes that.
theorems.proofSketch: Integrate \mu(x)=-d/dx[\ln S(x)] from 0 to x, using S(0)=1.
theorems.example: Given \mu(x)=1/(100-x), integrate to recover S(x)=(100-x)/100 (a De Moivre-type law).
theorems.examReady: Given mu(x), integrate then exponentiate; given S(x), differentiate and negate/divide.

theorems.name: Annuity-Due to Annuity-Immediate Relation
theorems.conditions: Same interest rate i and payment count n throughout.
theorems.intuition: Every due-annuity payment happens exactly one period earlier than its immediate-annuity counterpart.
theorems.proofSketch: Multiply every discounted term of a_n by (1+i), or split off the first due payment.
theorems.example: A 5-year annuity-due of 1000/year at 6% equals (1.06) times the corresponding annuity-immediate value.
theorems.examReady: Identify immediate vs. due from payment timing, apply the (1+i) conversion factor.
